intent: Hold the open state of one popover and tie its trigger to the floating panel it opens beside it.
typical_uses: A small panel of controls opened from a button, such as a filter or the settings of one field
Supplementary interactive content the user opens deliberately and dismisses when done

dont_use_when.situation: A list of actions anchored to a trigger
A short, non-interactive label for a control
A preview of what a link points to, shown on hover
A task that must block the rest of the page until the user finishes it

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

With `modal` at its default `false` the page stays scrollable and interactive while the popover is open. `true` locks page scroll and lays the primitive's transparent blocking layer over the page, except when the popover was opened by hover; `'trap-focus'` does neither. Either value traps focus in the popup only while a close part of the primitive (Popover.Close) is rendered inside it, and the kit exports none, so a popover built from kit parts alone never traps focus.

Escape and a press outside the popup close the popover, reporting the reason to `onOpenChange`; while focus is not trapped, focus moving from the trigger or the popup to an element outside both closes it too, unless the popover was opened by hover.

children.states: children is the root's content, either React nodes or a function of the active trigger's payload that returns them
children.because: `React.ReactNode | PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` - the function form receives `{ payload }` from whichever trigger opened the popover. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, and a function has no JSON Schema representation.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (a trigger press, hover or focus, an outside press, Escape, a close press, focus moving out or an imperative action). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with imperative `close` and `unmount` actions
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<PopoverRootActions | null>` - a ref object holding functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Popover.createHandle(), shared with a trigger placed outside this root
handle.because: `PopoverHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the popover's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

modal.states: modal is true, false or the string 'trap-focus'
modal.because: `boolean | 'trap-focus'` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a boolean-or-string union is left unasserted.

triggerId.states: triggerId is the id of the trigger a controlled popover is open for, or null
triggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

defaultTriggerId.states: defaultTriggerId is the id of the trigger an initially open popover is open for, or null
defaultTriggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

good.title: A panel of settings opened from a button
good.code:
<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Dimensions</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <PopoverHeader>
      <PopoverTitle>Dimensions</PopoverTitle>
      <PopoverDescription>Set the dimensions for the layer.</PopoverDescription>
    </PopoverHeader>
    <Input aria-label="Width" defaultValue="100%" />
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>

good.title: A popover opened from state the caller owns

bad.title: A controlled popover nothing can close
bad.why: Without `onOpenChange` nothing turns `open` false, so neither the trigger, Escape nor an outside press closes the popover.
